event_description: The Fluent Connect widget mounted on a partner page. Denominator for every funnel; guarded to fire once per page load regardless of how many times React mounts the widget. Carries has_stored_session, which splits returning visitors from new ones.
The connect modal was opened. The trigger property separates a real connect-button click from a re-authorisation forced by the faucet.
User picked how to connect. The method property is fluent or external; for external, wallet names the button pressed — the Reown modal that opens next may end in a different wallet.
Fluent login was requested — the direct Privy flow started, or the hosted popup was asked to open. Fires on click, so a popup blocked by the browser still counts as started.

A Fluent session was applied in the widget. Fires in both hosted and direct auth modes. Client-side and therefore forgeable; the authoritative count is the server-side session_issued event (FLU-1119). From this event onward every event also carries smart_account_address and embedded_wallet_address.
Login did not produce a session. The reason property is one of hosted_error, state_mismatch, origin_mismatch, smart_account_missing, direct_auth_failed. Never carries a raw error message.

An external wallet connected after the user picked it in the connect modal — the terminal step of the non-Fluent branch. Not reported for a wallet wagmi restores on load, one a partner hands the widget already connected, or a WalletConnect session that re-establishes itself. Carries chain_id when the wallet reports one.

User asked to disconnect, from the wallet menu button or the account dropdown. Emitted at those entry points rather than inside the teardown, because re-login (Connect with X) tears the session down first and is not a disconnect.

A wallet-menu tab was left: on tab switch, on drawer close, and on page hide. Carries tab and dwell_ms. "Opened a tab and did nothing" is derived per $session_id by the absence of any other wallet_* event between two of these.
The faucet request failed. The reason property is session_expired (the 401 refresh branch) or request_failed.
The silent-signing switch on the settings tab was flipped. Carries enabled.
A gas payment token was chosen on the settings tab. Carries symbol.

User left the widget for another site — bridge or explorer. Carries label, destination_domain and surface (wallet_menu or account_menu) instead of one event name per destination. Fires before the popup is attempted, so a blocked popup still counts.

Not an event. Every event above carries client_id, network, auth_mode, source, campaign and sdk_version; once a session exists it also carries smart_account_address and embedded_wallet_address, including a session restored from localStorage — on a returning visit those addresses are already attached to widget_loaded. These are applied after the event's own properties, so an event cannot overwrite them.
